Verbos com preposição, passo a passo: Verbs with prepositions, step by step
PASSO 1: muitos verbos alemães pedem uma: STEP 1: many German verbs take a FIXED PREPOSITION that's part of the verb and can't be swapped: «warten AUF» (wait for), «denken AN» (think of), «sich interessieren FÜR» (be interested in). STEP 2: the preposition TAKES A CASE (accusative or dative), and the noun after it is in that case: «Ich warte auf DEN Bus» (accusative). STEP 3: ALWAYS learn the verb with its preposition and case: «warten auf + Akk». STEP 4: the German preposition is often NOT the one English uses: wait FOR = warten AUF; think OF = denken AN; interested IN = interessiert FÜR; depend ON = abhängen VON. Translating the English preposition is the #1 mistake. STEP 5: in this session, verbs with «AUF»: all take the ACCUSATIVE in their common uses: «Ich freue mich auf den Urlaub», «Ich hoffe auf gutes Wetter.» STEP 6: with a person, use the pronoun or noun in the accusative: «Ich warte auf meinen Bruder» / «Ich warte auf ihn.»
em português a preposição muda por verbo: English verbs have fixed prepositions too ("wait for", "think of", "depend on") — but they almost never match the German ones. Learn each German verb as a chunk: «warten auf», «denken an», «abhängen von».

Verbos com an, für e über: Verbs with an, für and über
PASSO 1: com «AN»: «denken an + Akk» («I: STEP 1: with «AN»: «denken an + Akk» («Ich denke an dich» — I'm thinking of you), «glauben an + Akk» («Ich glaube an dich» — I believe in you), «sich erinnern an + Akk» (remember), and «teilnehmen an + DATIVE» («Ich nehme an dem Kurs teil» — «am Kurs» — I'm taking part in the course). STEP 2: with «FÜR»: always accusative: «sich interessieren für + Akk» («Ich interessiere mich für Musik» — interested IN = für), «sich entscheiden für + Akk» (decide on), «sich bedanken für + Akk» (thank for). STEP 3: with «ÜBER»: accusative: «sprechen über + Akk» (talk about), «sich ärgern über + Akk» (be annoyed about), «sich freuen über + Akk» (be happy about something you have), «diskutieren über + Akk». STEP 4: remember the difference: «freuen auf» (future, look forward to) × «freuen über» (present, be glad about). STEP 5: a trick: «über» = about the topic, «für» = interest or support, «an» = a mental connection.
